title: Remove Linked List Elements
description:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list and an integer `val`, remove all nodes of the linked list that have `Node.val == val`, and return the new head of the modified list.

If all nodes are removed or the input list is empty, return `null` (`None` in Python).
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 10^4].
hints: Attach a sentinel dummy node before `head` so removing the original head node follows the exact same pointer update as removing any interior node.
Advance the `curr` pointer only when `curr.next.val != val`; when deleting `curr.next`, re-link `curr.next = curr.next.next` and inspect the new successor on the next iteration.

examples.explanation: Both nodes with value 6 (at positions 3 and 7) are removed, leaving [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].
An empty list has no nodes to remove, so return null.
Every node has value 7, so removing all of them produces an empty list (null).
